newsitem.title: USA: FERC queries schedule for Maritimes, Portland pipe.
newsitem.headline: FERC queries schedule for Maritimes, Portland pipe.

text.p: The U.S. Federal Energy Regulatory Commission Friday questioned the rapid schedule outlined by Portland Natural Gas Transmission System and Maritimes & Northeast Pipeline in their plan to build a natural gas pipeline from Maine to Massachusetts.
Maritimes and Portland Natural Gas were set to file a proposal later this month to build a jointly-owned pipeline to serve new customers and eventually import gas from Canada's Sable Island.
The proposal would merge what had been competing pipeline plans by the two groups in order to limit environmental harm.

The commission Friday told Maritimes and Portland Natural Gas to explain in their upcoming filing why they needed to have construction approval as soon as August 31 and be up and running in 1998, a FERC spokeswoman said following a technical conference at the commission.
Under the approval schedule envisioned by Maritimes and Portland Natural Gas, the commission would have to give a preliminary nod to the new pipeline plan in February.

Portland Natural Gas Transmission System is owned by Bay State Gas Co, El Paso Energy, MCN Corp, Gaz Metropolitain and Co LP, TransCanada PipeLines Ltd, and US Generating Co, co-owned by Pacific Gas and Electric Co and Bechtel Group Inc.
Maritimes and Northeast is owned by PanEnergy Corp, Westcoast Energy Inc, Eastern Enterprises and Mobil Corp.
